svg.aria-label: Privacy and permissions. Not offline: Local interface does not mean offline agent: OMP may send prompts and tool context to your chosen provider, and tools and MCP servers may make their own network requests Model lists: When it starts, OMP asks several outside services for their public model catalogues and probes local model servers on this Mac. This is OMP's own behaviour, in a terminal as in Null No listener: Null has no HTTP listener and no database of its own; it starts the OMP it carries as a child process and talks over stdio Credentials: Your /login answers go to the local omp login process, are masked in the UI and are never written to Null's settings or log. OMP handles authentication; no Null account exists Attached files: Null reads no file's content. A file you attach goes to the harness as its full path, which travels to your provider with the message, your user name in it. The content follows only when the agent reads the file Conversations: OMP keeps your conversations, one file each. To find one by something said in it, Null reads those files on this Mac as you type in /history, keeps nothing of them and logs no word. Deleting moves a conversation's file to the Mac's Trash, where it can be put back, and changes nothing in it Shortcut: Control+Space needs no Accessibility or Input Monitoring permission. If registration fails, the box opens with a notice Approvals: Null passes on OMP's approval setting and adds none of its own. OMP's own default lets the agent act without asking you first, and the first opening says so Computer use: Off until you switch it on with /computer. Then the agent may read what any window holds and press and type in any app, and, with Screen Recording, take pictures of the screen. OMP does this, not Null: Null neither looks at the screen nor keeps what the agent saw. While it is on, Null also tells the agent its own rules for working a Mac: the ways in, few turns, and leaving your things alone. They are the same for everyone and say nothing about you. It follows OMP's approval setting like any other tool, so with OMP's default the agent uses your Mac without asking you first. Set to ask, this OMP cannot put its question through the box and refuses computer use Verifying: Off until you name a model with /verify. Then, when a reply that took steps has ended, Null moves that conversation to the model you named, sends it one message of Null's own that asks it to check the answer against what was seen, and puts the conversation back. While a backup is answering, the conversation is not moved: the model that answered is asked instead. It is the only message Null sends that you did not type, and the box says so each time. Conversations started with /folder are left alone Its permissions: Two: Accessibility and Screen Recording, which macOS charges to Null because Null starts the agent. Null asks macOS for them only when you switch computer use on or choose one in the /computer list, never at a start. Screen Recording may be left off: the agent then reads and presses, and has no pictures Full Disk Access: A separate choice, asked once, after the first reply, with an explanation: macOS attributes the agent's file access to Null. It is broader file access, not a sandbox, and it does not replace OMP's approval rules. The box opens without it

g.text: Privacy and permissions
Not offline
Local interface does not mean offline agent: OMP may send prompts and tool
context to your chosen provider, and tools and MCP servers may make their own
network requests
Model lists
When it starts, OMP asks several outside services for their public model
catalogues and probes local model servers on this Mac. This is OMP's own
behaviour, in a terminal as in Null
No listener
Null has no HTTP listener and no database of its own; it starts the OMP it
carries as a child process and talks over stdio
Credentials
Your /login answers go to the local omp login process, are masked in the UI and
are never written to Null's settings or log. OMP handles authentication; no Null
account exists
Attached files
Null reads no file's content. A file you attach goes to the harness as its full
path, which travels to your provider with the message, your user name in it. The
content follows only when the agent reads the file
Conversations
OMP keeps your conversations, one file each. To find one by something said in it,
Null reads those files on this Mac as you type in /history, keeps nothing of them
and logs no word. Deleting moves a conversation's file to the Mac's Trash, where
it can be put back, and changes nothing in it
Shortcut
Control+Space needs no Accessibility or Input Monitoring permission. If
registration fails, the box opens with a notice
Approvals
Null passes on OMP's approval setting and adds none of its own. OMP's own default
lets the agent act without asking you first, and the first opening says so
Computer use
Off until you switch it on with /computer. Then the agent may read what any
window holds and press and type in any app, and, with Screen Recording, take
pictures of the screen. OMP does this, not Null: Null neither looks at the screen
nor keeps what the agent saw. While it is on, Null also tells the agent its own
rules for working a Mac: the ways in, few turns, and leaving your things alone.
They are the same for everyone and say nothing about you. It follows OMP's
approval setting like any other tool, so with OMP's default the agent uses your
Mac without asking you first. Set to ask, this OMP cannot put its question
through the box and refuses computer use
Verifying
Off until you name a model with /verify. Then, when a reply that took steps has
ended, Null moves that conversation to the model you named, sends it one message
of Null's own that asks it to check the answer against what was seen, and puts
the conversation back. While a backup is answering, the conversation is not
moved: the model that answered is asked instead. It is the only message Null
sends that you did not type, and the box says so each time. Conversations started
with /folder are left alone
Its permissions
Two: Accessibility and Screen Recording, which macOS charges to Null because Null
starts the agent. Null asks macOS for them only when you switch computer use on
or choose one in the /computer list, never at a start. Screen Recording may be
left off: the agent then reads and presses, and has no pictures
Full Disk Access
A separate choice, asked once, after the first reply, with an explanation: macOS
attributes the agent's file access to Null. It is broader file access, not a
sandbox, and it does not replace OMP's approval rules. The box opens without it
